lines: Zipline CEO Keller Cliffton argues that every 10x jump in scale forces a full reinvention of processes, manufacturing and org structure, so the company runs with 'no sacred cows'.

Because autonomous flight was illegal in US airspace, Zipline launched in Rwanda in 2016 with life-saving deliveries such as blood; the episode cites a 51% reduction in maternal mortality as proof the model works.

After more than 3 million deliveries, Zipline is expanding in the US; Cliffton contends fast, reliable autonomous delivery could grow the US instant-delivery market from about 5.5 billion to 50 billion deliveries a year.
He favors small, empowered 'special forces' teams over hierarchy, and says users normalize seemingly sci-fi services within about a week, while early real-world flaws are a sign of fast iteration.
title: What Breaks When You Scale 10x? | Zipline’s Keller Cliffton
